pr_title: Fix failure to dispose stream when exception occurs in Package.Open
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46791

Note these tests run against .NET Framework as well, demonstrating indeed it is a regression. (On .NET Framework, the garbling produces ArgumentOutOfRangeException, but it does dispose the stream.)

This test will pass even with the bug if the finalizer thread is lucky, but in my tests it consistently fails without the fix.

issue_context.title: File not released when exception occurs in Package.Open
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

When I try to call `Package.Open` on an invalid package (file attached), the file lock is not released. The subsequent `File.Move` throws an `IOException`: `The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process`

```c#
using System.IO;
using System.IO.Packaging;

internal class Program
{
    private static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        try
        {
            using var package = Package.Open("PdfWithFakeExtension.xlsx", FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.Read);
        }
        catch
        {
            // Swallow exception
        }

        File.Move("PdfWithFakeExtension.xlsx", @"C:\temp\PdfWithFakeExtension.xlsx");
    }
}

```
### Configuration


* Which version of .NET is the code running on?
`netcore3.1`

* What OS and version, and what distro if applicable?
`System.IO.Packaging` version 5.0.0
* What is the architecture (x64, x86, ARM, ARM64)?
`AnyCPU`


### Regression?

Yes, I think this is a regression. Using a `net472` build and using `WindowsBase` instead of the `System.IO.Packaging` NuGet package, the file is released, so I don't experience this problem.


### Other information

[PdfWithFakeExtension.xlsx](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/files/5792595/PdfWithFakeExtension.xlsx)
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

> * Which version of .NET is the code running on?
>   `netstandard2.1`

This doesn't refer to the target framework of the library containing this, but the entry executable. Should be .NET Core 3.x or .NET 5. netstandard isn't runnable.

> > * Which version of .NET is the code running on?
> >   `netstandard2.1`
> 
> This doesn't refer to the target framework of the library containing this, but the entry executable. Should be .NET Core 3.x or .NET 5. netstandard isn't runnable.

Updated to `netcore3.1`

In .NET Framework the stream is closed on exception here
https://referencesource.microsoft.com/#WindowsBase/Base/MS/Internal/IO/Zip/ZipArchive.cs,109

The .NET Core code seems to have a different heritage as it is rather different, and it does not close the stream here
https://source.dot.net/#System.IO.Packaging/System/IO/Packaging/ZipPackage.cs,283

If the object had been successfully created, it would have closed the stream in Dispose().
As a workaround @igitur you could of course create your own FileStream around the path, and hand Package.Open that stream.

> As a workaround @igitur you could of course create your own FileStream around the path, and hand Package.Open that stream.

I wondered whether that would work. (I'm the person on behalf of whom @igitur raised the issue here.) But although that would allow me always to unlock the file, might it just shift the problem to the FileStream, leaving it undisposed (or leaving me unable to dispose of it) and creating a leak? In other words, is this problem also present in the constructor that takes a stream argument as well as in the one that takes a file path argument?

@HalHaynes 

>  In other words, is this problem also present in the constructor that takes a stream argument as well as in the one that takes a file path argument?

I don't think so. That code flow is
https://source.dot.net/#System.IO.Packaging/System/IO/Packaging/Package.cs,905
to
https://source.dot.net/#System.IO.Packaging/System/IO/Packaging/ZipPackage.cs,348
the true in `zipArchive = new ZipArchive(s, zipArchiveMode, true, Text.Encoding.UTF8);` is a boolean `leaveOpen`. It indicates that ZipArchive should not close the stream when disposed.

As for ZipPackage, it sets a boolean `_shouldCloseContainerStream` to false here
https://source.dot.net/#System.IO.Packaging/System/IO/Packaging/ZipPackage.cs,368
which in turn means that it will not close the stream when disposed.

I think in general it is unusual for an API to close a stream it is passed. I would think that is normally the responsibility of the caller, who may have other things they wish to do with the stream.

LMK if you hit a problem.

Note that this fix would be for .NET 6 to release in November. With a reasonable workaround, I don't believe this would meet the bar to service older versions.

BTW welcome to our repo @HalHaynes
Thanks! I tried the work-around and it was successful.
